answer: Hardware-rooted attestation curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to generate credentials inside secure enclaves running a cryptographic cipher. To deploy counterfeit nodes, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing physical security chips for each instance, whether an agent tracks raven nesting or manages vine irrigation. This enforces a real capital floor per identity, but it introduces reliance on proprietary chip foundries and vulnerability to side-channel exploits.
